_comment: Pinned dependency versions for Whispers.
Nothing here is ever resolved as 'latest' at run time: every artefact is
fetched at the exact tag below and rejected unless its SHA-256 matches.
Raising a pin is a deliberate act: edit this file, re-run tools/validate,
then publish. See README.md, section 'Raising a pinned version'.
Where Whispers looks for a newer version of itself, and the
suffix of the asset to install. Remove this block to turn update
checking off for every install; a user can also turn it off for
their own machine from the settings window.
Unlike every other pin here, an update cannot carry a SHA-256
recorded in advance - the release does not exist yet. The hash is
read from GitHub's API response and used to reject a corrupted
download. See README.md, 'What the update check does and does not
guarantee'.
Binaries live on bNNNN build tags. The semantic vX.Y.Z tags carry no
assets from v1.9.3 onward - pinning 'v1.9.4' would download nothing.
b5130 was published the same day as v1.9.4 (2026-09-11).
Each CUDA archive bundles its own cudart/cublas DLLs, so the target
machine needs an NVIDIA driver but no CUDA Toolkit.
Shipped alongside Whispers.ahk rather than installed system-wide:
the official interpreter is a binary every antivirus already knows,
whereas an Ahk2Exe-compiled script trips their packer heuristics.
Raising this pin means re-running BOTH test suites, because the
interpreter is what executes every line of the product.
What the settings window and the first-run setup need to host
their pages in WebView2 (ADR-0001): thqby's AutoHotkey v2 binding,
the two files of the same library it includes, and the x64
WebView2Loader.dll it ships, which is Microsoft's own, signed.
Fetched from the repository at this exact commit, never 'master',
by tools/fetch-vendor.ps1 into vendor/, and built into the
installer: they are part of the program rather than something to
download on the user's machine. The fetch also checks that the DLL
carries a valid Microsoft Authenticode signature.
The WebView2 runtime itself is not pinned: it belongs to Windows,
which updates it. See README.md, 'WebView2'.
Tiers are named by user benefit, not by model name: the user never
picks a file. Measured on an i9-12900K / RTX 4070 Ti, 11 s of audio,
model load included - see README.md for the full table.
'cpu' is forced on machines without a usable NVIDIA GPU: the turbo
models share large-v3's encoder, so they bring no CPU speedup.
